On NAND supply: 'we still able to get supply, but unfortunately supply not enough to what we need... We have supply, but supply still not enough what we need.' Phison met every NAND supplier at FMS last week and pitched that its purchases feed its own AI data-platform systems, not just module resale; it will not disclose how many LTAs it holds so competitors cannot ask for the same amounts. CEO expects the NAND shortage to continue into next year and beyond ('many year'); a top NAND-maker executive told him a new fab takes 4 years from investment to production, not 2. Downgrade-grade NAND supply is also shrinking structurally: 3D NAND yields now run 90-plus percent, with some wafers at 95% good die, so the cheap downgrade bin that used to feed consumer products is disappearing.
new NAND fab: 4 years investment-to-production; 3D NAND yields 90%+ (some wafers 95%)

NAND pricing/margin view: back in March the CEO said NAND makers' gross margin reaching a floor of 80% was easy and 85% might happen; now he says 90% gross margin may happen in 2026, but warns that is unhealthy for the industry ('if you ask component for 90% gross margin, industry potentially will be killed - you can see the IoT, you can see the consumer die'). Demand is too strong, so price will keep rising but at a decelerating rate toward saturation, at which point suppliers start choosing whom to ship. On demand structure: systems have cut DRAM content ('a lot of systems, they cut half of the DRAM') but nobody cuts storage - inference needs storage, 'storage is money' - and aiDAPTIV uses flash to complement DRAM.
NAND-maker gross margin: 80% floor easy, 85% may happen, 90% possible in 2026 (CEO view)

New design wins in the quarter per the prepared remarks: 6 new design wins in AI networking (including one described as a very large program), 2 new neocloud design wins, plus new wins across CSP, server OEM, AI storage systems, infrastructure, and the AI-chip ecosystem, in both boot-drive and main-drive sockets; most of the limited NAND supply goes into customized products, which is why margins beat commodity module makers. The E37 enterprise controller, described as world-best performance, has won several large OEM programs.
6 new AI-networking design wins; 2 new neocloud design wins

Next growth leg is the transition from controller/module vendor to systems vendor: the Phison aiDAPTIV AI data platform (own-defined storage servers built on Phison SSDs with in-house software) should start showing significant numbers from CQ4 2026 through CQ1-CQ2 2027, with a bigger reveal promised next quarter ('hopefully I can show you our big transformation within 12 to 24 months'). For AI-on-device, Phison partners with Intel and MediaTek (versus AMD working with Longsys): a POC with MediaTek uses Phison's UFS4 controller to cut a phone's required LPDDR5 from 24GB to 12GB while keeping AI-model performance, targeted at the market next year. Product cadence: PCIe Gen5 controllers already in mass production; the first PCIe Gen6 controller is going to mass production directly without any ECO, with November cited as the timing.
MediaTek UFS4 POC cuts required LPDDR5 from 24GB to 12GB; Gen6 controller to MP with no ECO (November cited)

Inventory and funding: in June-July Phison spent more than $450 million of cash buying NAND wafers from Shenzhen module houses that were dumping consumer-heavy inventory at prices well below NAND-maker contract prices ('don't take this as price decrease - the NAND guys are not going to decline their price'). Inventory of roughly 90 billion (NT$, book value) is carried at cost and never revalued upward, only written down. Balance sheet: the large bank debt outstanding at end-March was almost fully repaid by July ('now we have no debt'); the $800 million ECB raised earlier has already been deployed into NAND ('already turned one and a half times'); if business keeps growing strongly, new fundraising may be needed in the second half of next year.
$450M+ NAND wafer purchases in June-July; inventory ~90 billion NT (book value); $800M ECB deployed

→ CoreWeave: CEO Mike Intrator cited CoreWeave's 'recent long-term agreement with Solidigm' as an illustration of how it is derisking access to the critical inputs needed to serve customers, alongside its close partnerships with NVIDIA and its OEM and ODM partners. He described a supply chain spanning land, power and shell through GPUs, networking and MEMORY, all of it being challenged by the growth of AI, and CFO Nitin Agrawal named Solidigm again as a new partner relationship used to strategically source required inputs amid a complex global supply chain.

Enterprise storage is now an explicit growth and margin vector: expanded enterprise CPU-based server, STORAGE and IoT product lines since early 2026, and Q4 enterprise/channel revenue of $5.6B (50% of total, +172% YoY) came from customers upgrading compute, STORAGE and network infrastructure. Enterprise storage is one of the pillars of the DCBBS total solution (GPU + CPU server, enterprise storage, DLC, switching, management software, lifecycle service), and storage/CPU/IoT carry higher gross margin than high-volume GPU platforms.
Enterprise & channel $5.6B (50% of Q4 rev, +172% YoY) incl. storage upgrades

NAND: a little activity but no trend yet; anyone with clean room space is using it for higher-value DRAM. Vertical scaling of NAND does not change implant density, so NAND only helps Axcelis when customers add wafer capacity; historically NAND has followed DRAM. Memory systems carry lower-than-corporate-average gross margin but drive higher-margin CS&I aftermarket over the tool life.

Growth catalysts: GAA sales were about JPY 5 billion in Q1 and are expected at over JPY 20 billion for FY March 2027. Advanced packaging revenue, JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026, is now expected at JPY 15 billion in FY March 2027 (Q1 was JPY 4.5 billion) - a significant upward revision from the JPY 6 billion prior plan, driven by both rising customer CapEx and additional POR wins for its film deposition technology. In NAND, demand-supply is not fully adjusted - memory players are allocating clean room to DRAM while NAND wafer output needs to increase - so greenfield NAND investments are expected to resume, which converts all of Kokusai's PORs to sales and is broadly favorable. In DRAM, the D1C transition is complete and D1D is progressing. NAND sales could approach record highs, and DRAM plus NAND plus advanced packaging support growth above WFE (targeting more than a 20% sales increase).
GAA JPY 5 billion in Q1, over JPY 20 billion FY March 2027; advanced packaging raised to JPY 15 billion FY March 2027 from JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026

Front-end memory metrology also inflected: advanced-nodes revenue reached ~$120M (+50% QoQ, a record beating the prior 2022 peak) and MEMORY is ~60% of that, growing ~60% sequentially, with DRAM and NAND (off a small base) both up. Onto expects to ship MULTIPLE ATLAS G6 SYSTEMS TO A MAJOR DRAM CUSTOMER in H2 2026 to support next-generation memory devices - the first DRAM customers to adopt the platform, following the gate-all-around logic customers named last quarter. Atlas G6's smaller spot size lets customers apply OCD inside the die rather than only on scribe-line test structures
advanced nodes ~$120M (+50% QoQ); memory ~60% of it, +~60% QoQ; Atlas G6 to a major DRAM customer in H2

ADVANCED-NODES REVENUE ~$120M, +50% SEQUENTIALLY - a new record surpassing the previous peak set in 2022 - with logic up more than 40% QoQ and memory ~60% QoQ. Full-year advanced-nodes growth outlook RAISED to MORE THAN 35% (from ~25% guided last quarter), explicitly 'continuing to outpace the latest WFE growth expectations' (analysts were framing WFE at $190-200B, ~+30%). Mix has shifted from a historical thirds split across DRAM/logic/NAND toward roughly 50% logic / 50% memory
advanced nodes ~$120M, +50% QoQ (record); FY26 growth raised to +>35%

Memory: shipments rose 8.8% sequentially to $34 million after strong growth the prior quarter, currently focused on delivering NAND technology and capacity. Management stated that DATA CENTER IS NOW THE LARGEST END APPLICATION ACROSS GLOBAL NAND PRODUCTION, with about 40% of the NAND market going to data centers. Beyond NAND, the vertical wire team continues to work closely with memory customers as they develop NEW FORMS OF STACKED DRAM applications.
Memory $34M (+8.8% QoQ); ~40% of the NAND market goes to data centers

NAND is turning: MKS saw increased momentum in NAND UPGRADE activity in Q2 and expects it to continue, possibly better. RF power is the LARGEST PART OF THE BILL OF MATERIALS in such an upgrade, which is why MKS benefits disproportionately from upgrades. Announced NAND GREENFIELD fabs are expected to come in towards the END OF 2027 AND BEGINNING OF 2028, which would be even better because MKS would supply the rest of its semiconductor portfolio around a brand-new tool; NAND should become a bigger percentage of semi revenue in 2028. Until then the mix stays largely logic and DRAM driven.
NAND greenfield fabs expected end-2027 into 2028; NAND to become a bigger share of semi revenue in 2028

CALL — GUIDE RAISED A THIRD TIME; SUPPLY CHAIN REBUILT: FY2026 revenue raised to ~$12.6B = 40% GROWTH (+$2.1B vs the $10.5B Analyst Day plan, +$1.1B vs May's $11.5B) — the raise deliberately UNALLOCATED across AI fabrics (goal >=$3.5B), campus (>=$1.25B), core front-end data center ('isn't going to be flat' — enterprise, new logos, international) and routing; operating margin RAISED to 48-49% (Q2 hit 49.9%). Supply chain: Jayshree — 'the INDUSTRY is going to have a TWO-YEAR problem... I don't think we get out of it as an industry TILL 2028,' but Arista's specific H1 actions pay off in H2: MULTI-YEAR PURCHASE COMMITMENTS NEARLY TRIPLED YoY to $9.7 BILLION (from $3.6B; $8.9B in Q1); MEMORY SUPPLY SECURED FOR 2026 with visibility WELL INTO 2027 (DDR4/DDR5/NAND); PCB + optics capacity buildable in a 12-month window; a NEW LIQUID-COOLING SUPPLY CHAIN stood up (cold plates, quick disconnects, tubing with capacity agreements); 3 CMs + 3 distribution hubs (US/Asia/Mexico). Guidance is explicitly supply-gated: 'guiding based on what we're CONFIDENT we can get the supply for — if supply released more, there is opportunity to do better.' Price increases only help 'end of the year or more like next year' (backlog); FY GM held 62-64% including memory/silicon cost inflation. Etherlink AI-fabric customers now EXCEED 100 CUMULATIVE (from 4-5 in 2024).
FY26 raised to ~$12.6B (+40%, 3rd raise); purchase commitments ~3x YoY to $9.7B; memory secured into 2027; liquid-cooling chain built; >100 AI customers

Fab utilization: advanced logic tracking to the mid-80% range, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%; every wafer at advanced nodes requires more layers, more processing complexity and more packaging steps, translating to more Qnity content.
utilization: advanced logic mid-80%, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%

Magnetic Application Products: net sales JPY 81.6 billion +49.6% YoY, operating profit JPY 9.6 billion +51.8% - HDD market demand remains strong on expanding AI data center demand; HDD head shipment volume +36% and HDD suspension shipment volume +31% YoY (QoQ heads +12%, suspensions +8%). R&D expenses rising in the HDD head business advancing next-generation technologies such as HAMR. Sensor Application Products sales JPY 61.9 billion +33.3% with OP JPY 7.8 billion (~3x); Energy Application Products sales JPY 405.8 billion +42.1% with OP JPY 69.4 billion +25.3% (small-battery price adjustments, battery pack expansion, mid-sized industrial batteries; JPY 2.6 billion one-time gain on EV power supply business transfer).
Magnetic sales JPY 81.6 billion +49.6%; HDD head shipments +36%, suspensions +31% YoY on AI data center demand

Product momentum in FY2027: coater developer (share of more than 90% across EUV to immersion lithography) won PORs in multiple processes in advanced logic and DRAM with the new Resive Pro Dice; full-year etch system sales of JPY 1 trillion are coming within reach; cryogenic etch systems for 400-layer NAND start deploying in customers' mass production lines from calendar 2027; a POR was won for a new low resistance metal deposition system in a new application area. For DRAM interconnect etch, five-year cumulative sales to fiscal 2030 are getting closer to JPY 1 trillion, significantly exceeding the original guidance of JPY 500 billion. In advanced packaging, prober sales show outstanding growth with full-year sales likely to go significantly beyond JPY 100 billion, and the Prexa SDP device prober for advanced logic launched in April; bonder/debonder and 3D-IC are growth areas combining leading-edge front-end and bonding technology.

Coater developer share more than 90%; etch sales JPY 1 trillion full-year within reach; DRAM interconnect etch five-year cumulative sales near JPY 1 trillion vs JPY 500 billion original guidance; prober sales significantly beyond JPY 100 billion; cryogenic etch for 400 layers in mass production from calendar 2027

AI data center applications drive the WFE market: sales to AI data center are expected to grow by five times or more in the five years from calendar 2023 through calendar 2027, spanning not only GPU and HBM but also DDR, CPU and 3D NAND. Technology transitions expected within two years: logic scaling from the 3 nanometer mainstream toward 2 nanometer with backside PDN adoption, DRAM evolving to the 1D node (1C to 1D transition), HBM stacked DRAM count rising from 12 to 16, and NAND evolving to 300 layers and further to 400 layers. Agentic AI is the driver of the overall WFE market; CY2026 WFE application mix is about 60% logic and 40% memory, versus 65%/35% last year.
AI data center WFE sales to grow five times or more CY2023-CY2027; HBM stacks from 12 to 16; NAND to 300 then 400 layers; logic mainstream 3 nanometer moving to 2 nanometer

CALL — TRAINIUM MERCHANT-SILICON DOOR OPENS; OWN FRONTIER MODEL: 'An increasing number of customers are interested in us providing the Trainium chips to them, SEPARATE FROM OUR CLOUD, and we're actively having those conversations... I expect there's a REAL CHANCE we'll do that in the future' (Jassy). Trainium adopter list broadened beyond the Anthropic + OpenAI multi-year multi-gigawatt anchors: unicorns Neurorobotics and Odyssey join Twelve Labs, Descartes Labs, Poolside AI, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI and Splash Music, plus Uber and Pinterest. AI-pulls-core mechanism: post-training reinforcement learning and AGENT TOOL USE run mostly on CPUs → Graviton (30-40% better price-performance; Graviton5 ramping ~2x faster than Graviton4). Amazon IS pursuing its OWN FRONTIER MODEL — for cost control, training-priority control and speed — while keeping Bedrock model-agnostic: 'within the next few years you're going to have at least a half dozen models comparably good to each other... one of them will be ours.' Agentic layer: Kiro coding agent usage TRIPLED QoQ (up to 50% more cost-effective); AWS Continuum security agent launched (finds/validates/remediates code vulnerabilities); Bedrock Agents added policies, payments, web search. Amazon Leo: ~400 satellites in orbit, initial internet service THIS YEAR with 'meaningful revenue commitments' from enterprises/governments. Memory/HDD/SSD inflation: existing contracts keep agreed prices for their duration; NEW deals price in current component costs.
Trainium sales OUTSIDE the cloud 'a real chance'; own frontier model coming ('one of the half dozen will be ours'); Kiro 3x QoQ

CALL — HBM PROCESS-CONTROL INTENSITY 'RIVALS ADVANCED LOGIC': CFO Bren Higgins said HBM is 'a unique animal' for KLA — base-die CUSTOMIZATION, the integration of each DRAM in the stack, the ultimate device value and tighter performance specs are driving process-control intensity levels 'RIVALING WHAT WE SEE IN ADVANCED LOGIC' across some products; conventional DRAM intensity has improved but is NOT the same as HBM. 2027 memory setup: DRAM investment broad across conventional AND HBM with GREENFIELD FABS (whole new toolsets, not just upgrades) — 'given where prices are and how that translates into margins, the VALUE OF YIELD is pretty high,' plus rising EUV adoption in DRAM; even NAND gets some greenfield. Mix: September quarter memory = 27% of semi-PC systems (DRAM 90% / NAND 10%); memory share RISES in the December quarter and stays elevated through H1 2027. Cost side: the memory-pricing gross-margin headwind is ~100bps 'and probably a little bit more' and now expected to CONTINUE THROUGH 2027 (new memory procured at higher prices) before normalizing into a TAILWIND.
HBM PC intensity rivals advanced logic; DRAM greenfield + EUV in 2027; memory GM headwind ~100bps+ through 2027 then tailwind

Memory market: AI servers keep driving HBM demand and high-end memory packaging demand stays very strong; DRAM and NAND market demand and prices are rising together, with customers maximising output of committed capacity - customer revenue gains are mostly price-driven as supply is limited, but PTI's packaging volumes are still growing and utilisation keeps improving. Packaging material costs keep rising and PTI is passing them through to customers gradually (its customers are large long-term partners, so price adjustments are made carefully each quarter). AI-server eSSD demand keeps rising with shipments expanding QoQ and YoY.

WFE is expected to grow about 20% in calendar 2026 and a similar level in calendar 2027. Updated CY2026 growth by application: advanced logic foundry over 20%, DRAM over 25% (raised), NAND about 20% (raised from a bit less than 15%), power devices a bit less than 10%. Foundry AI-driven leading edge investment is the primary WFE driver; advanced DRAM and HBM are in shortage and even existing DDR is in shortage, so CapEx is going into both HBM and general DDR, with strong NAND investment also expected as data center demand recovers. Memory device makers are asking for accelerated delivery - demand is now stronger than SCREEN's current capacity. Average equipment lead time is about 4.2 months. Chinese demand for advanced AI-related tools is at record-high inquiry levels.
WFE about 20% growth in calendar 2026 and 2027; DRAM over 25%, NAND about 20%, advanced logic foundry over 20%; lead time 4.2 months; demand stronger than capacity

CALL-ONLY / DEMAND-SIDE READ ON THE MEMORY SHORTAGE: at the OSAT level the DRAM squeeze is now measurable in handset volumes - Amkor's ANDROID revenue fell 20% SEQUENTIALLY 'reflecting the impact of MEMORY SUPPLY DYNAMICS', and Q3 communications is guided down high-single-digits sequentially (against normal seasonality) partly on 'ongoing MEMORY SUPPLY CONSTRAINTS', with memory PRICING also expected to weigh on phone unit volumes this year. Capacity response: Amkor's phased Vietnam build-out is adding SiP and NAND MEMORY capacity, while Korea's freed floor space is redirected to computing/advanced-packaging programs.
Android -20% QoQ on memory supply; Vietnam adding SiP + NAND memory capacity

CALL-ONLY: ARIZONA PHASE I IS NOW FULLY COMMITTED - 'our projections now show phase I as fully committed', with future expansion phases under evaluation. Global build-out detail given on the call: KOREA - the new Songdo assembly & test building remains on schedule for completion by end-2026, and the GWANGJU campus expansion adds clean-room capacity for data-center and advanced-packaging growth 'in 2028 AND BEYOND'; VIETNAM, PORTUGAL and TAIWAN are taking incremental clean room and equipment installs; Vietnam is being built out in phases for SiP and NAND MEMORY capacity, and moving SiP out of Korea 'enables additional capacity for our rapidly scaling COMPUTING programs in Korea'. 2026 capex reaffirmed at $2.5-3.0B: 65-70% facilities expansion (including Arizona Phase I), 30-35% HDFO/test/other advanced packaging, remainder R&D and quality. The cost of that build is explicit: ramping, UNDERUTILIZED Arizona manufacturing will be a drag on BOTH gross margin and operating margin in 2028 - the reason the 2028 target model looks similar to 2026 despite the growth.
Arizona Phase I FULLY COMMITTED; capex $2.5-3.0B (65-70% facilities); Gwangju cleanroom for 2028+

Build-out (five largest sites): ABILENE TX 42% of capacity delivered, +35% more within 90 days, remainder the following quarter; SHACKLEFORD TX delivery 1H CY27 with 115MW power online >1 month early; DONA ANA COUNTY NM delivery 1H CY27 — design based on GIGAWATTS of clean BLOOM fuel cells; SALINE MI delivery 2H 2027 (network core ahead of schedule, end of CY26); PORT WASHINGTON WI delivery 2H CY27. Funding: FY27 net cash capex ~$70B EXCLUDING $20-25B of customer PREPAYMENTS (reported capex higher); ~$40B debt+equity raise in FY27 incl. the $20B ATM equity program; no additional debt in CY2026. Component-cost protection: fixed-price customer contracts ONLY when costs are locked — otherwise FLOATING-cost mechanisms pass through memory/SSD/HDD inflation.
5 mega-sites ramping (Abilene 42%+35%/90d); FY27 capex ~$70B net; floating-cost contracts shield margins

Record Q2 FY2026 revenue $10.7B (+40% YoY, +15% QoQ), non-GAAP EPS $0.79 (+108% YoY), free cash flow $915M, gross margin 36.9%, operating margin 13.3%. Orders more than doubled, far outpacing revenue, for a record company backlog. Raised FY2026 outlook to ~$3.40 non-GAAP EPS (+40%) and at least $3.5B FCF — two years ahead of the long-term plan. Cloud & AI segment revenue $7.7B (+23%); traditional server orders grew triple-digits on agentic-AI inferencing; DRAM/NAND inflation + supply constraints lifting server ASPs (working with silicon/memory partners on long-term supply).

Sequential revenue +15% reflects higher server ASPs from DRAM/NAND inflationary costs; networking products constrained by DDR4/DDR5 and wafer capacity ('supply chain is the name of the game in networking' — purchase commitments +40% sequentially). FY2026 guide assumes NO incremental supply; component costs expected elevated into 2027 until new fabs yield. Inferencing accelerating as a demand driver — 'a lot of these inferencing deployments will be done on CPUs', traditional-server orders up triple digits on agentic-AI/high-memory configs; by end of decade Neri expects MOST demand to be inferencing. FY2027 framework: revenue +8-12% with AI-systems revenue accelerating.
DRAM/NAND-driven ASPs; no incremental 2026 supply; FY27 +8-12%

Data-center optics ramp: on the receiver side both 100G and 200G products are in mass production and shipping, with 100G (i.e. 800G transceivers) the mainstay this year and 1.6T expected to be a breakout next year. On the transmit side, 400G lasers entered mass production in Q2 2026 (first design win back in March 2023), with volumes expected to multiply next year, and CW laser customers have been in mass production since Q4 2024. New applications: solar-cell substrates for drones and low-earth-orbit satellites (including radiation-resistant flexible solar panels, with an LEO satellite project this year), and VCSELs used as the heating source in HAMR HDDs - in development for two years, with a meaningful contribution expected next year and the year after.

receiver-side 100G and 200G in mass production; 800G the mainstay this year with a 1.6T breakout expected next year; transmit-side 400G in mass production from Q2; CW lasers in production since Q4 2024

Four AI pillars: (1) AI infrastructure scaling — clusters integrating GPUs/CPUs/DPUs/switches/NICs/memory fabrics across vendors (Ethernet, UALink, PCIe, NVMe) incl. rack-backplane characterization for next-gen scale-up networks; (2) SPEED TRANSITIONS — 800G deployments accelerating 1.6T adoption with rising 3.2T R&D; (3) optical/photonics technologies; (4) system-level emulation. At OFC Keysight demonstrated 1.6T physical-layer solutions with 20+ industry leaders (traffic emulation, link reliability, SerDes signal integrity) and ran the industry's FIRST public Ultra Ethernet Consortium interoperability demo WITH BROADCOM.
1.6T test w/ 20+ leaders at OFC; first UEC interop demo w/ Broadcom; 3.2T R&D rising

Product/strategy: HBM TC bonders (12/16-high stacking) remain the core. KEY DISCLOSURE: because the industry's HYBRID-BONDER development is DELAYED by technical hurdles, 20-high+ HBM stacking needs a new tool that can bond WIDER dies — Hanmi is about to launch the "WIDE TC BONDER" for next-gen HBM structures, while ALSO developing hybrid bonders (for HBM and for system-semiconductor stacking) in parallel. Portfolio extensions: 6-SIDE INSPECTION (pre/post-TC-bond HBM yield control), world-first two-in-one BOC+COB bonder (stacked GDDR, enterprise eSSD), entry into 2.5D PACKAGING (TC/FC/die bonders for interposer integration of HBM + base die + CPU/GPU), MSVP 8.0 saw/vision placement (world #1 since mid-2000s, boosted by larger PLP/chiplet panels), EMI Shield 2.0 X (#1 share). Disclosed customer list: SK Hynix, MICRON, ASE, Amkor, JCET, Huatian, TFME, Infineon, STMicro, PTI, Skyworks, Luxshare + Korean OSATs/Samsung Electro-Mechanics/LG Innotek.
WIDE TC bonder launch imminent (hybrid-bonder delay = TC extension); 2.5D packaging entry; Micron now a disclosed customer

Product positioning: CUBE PROBER — full inspection of HBM at the individual-stack level with precision vision (filing: AI-driven HBM demand surging; HBM market led by SK Hynix/Samsung/Micron) — plus TWP300/TWP300H probe stations targeting localization of a market dominated by Tokyo Electron, and expansion from memory test handlers into SoC handlers, SSD/burn-in/wafer test solutions.
Cube Prober = per-stack HBM full-inspection; probe-station localization vs TEL
SUMCO projects an uptick in NAND wafer demand ahead as part of robust overall 300mm demand driven by AI data centers (Q1 2026 view).

Wafer market outlook: semiconductor market sees continued strong AI growth and only gradual recovery elsewhere. 300mm demand strong for leading-edge logic and DRAM in AI data centers with a projected NAND uptick ahead; recovery in non-leading-edge logic is gradual and partly TEMPERED BY MEMORY SHORTAGES (memory supply constraints curb non-leading-edge logic demand). 200mm and smaller lacks momentum, inventory-adjustment progress varies by customer.
AI leading-edge strong vs non-AI gradual; memory shortage caps non-leading-edge logic

Communications +33% QoQ on power solutions for optical modules and switches; storage strong (DDR5, HDD/SSD) pulled by data center; sampled first high-speed DDR5 interface products at major customers; CPU a continued tailwind; robotics / physical AI emerging

Memory: Aehr achieved the correlation a key memory supplier asked for and is discussing system specs for its next-generation flash and high bandwidth flash; it hopes to close in the next few months on a development agreement, followed by a 12- to 18-month development of memory-optimized blades for FOX-XP/NP. It is also in discussions with other memory suppliers that produce HBM (CEO sees 'interesting challenges' in HBM 4E suited to wafer-level burn-in); management believes memory 'could drive orders in fiscal '27 with ramps in fiscal '28'.
12- to 18-month development; orders possible in fiscal '27, ramps in fiscal '28

3D NAND: ACM's proprietary N2 bubbling wet etch is positioned for 3D NAND silicon nitride etching, where larger bubble size and uniformity control become more critical at 300 layer and above; the CEO said it covers today's 300-layer demand and addresses uniformity issues as the industry moves to 400 or even 500 layer, with demand seen both in China and globally.
300 layer and above; 400 or even 500 layer

Data storage: customers are adopting Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording (HAMR), raising capital intensity and CapEx; Veeco is fully booked for system orders for 2026 and has started booking orders into 2027. The first round of orders shipping in 2026 is for front-end fabs, and new orders are now arriving for back-end slider fabs for shipment in 2027 - a function of the number of heads shipping - giving 'legs into '27 and potentially beyond.'
Data storage fully booked for 2026; slider fab orders for 2027 shipment

Technology drivers (CEO): industry projections suggest semiconductors could reach $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2027, possibly earlier. Leading-edge fabs are deploying new materials like molybdenum and new structures such as gate-all-around and high-bandwidth memory, raising deposition/etch capex intensity. UCT expects strength around etch and deposition, especially ALD and high-precision etch, to support gate-all-around and backside power distribution logic transitions as well as high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging and greater than 300-layer NAND. A multiyear WFE upturn should follow once wafer fabs address their near-term clean room constraints.
semiconductor market $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2027 (industry projection); greater than 300-layer NAND

Memory cycle (CEO): some of UCT's customers' customers say the shortage will last until 2028; Micron, Samsung and SK are investing in greenfield fabs while converting existing fabs to address immediate demand, a multiyear upturn for memory. HBM will compromise the nameplate capacity in DRAM factories, so more WFE investment is needed to compensate while makers still address the unbalanced supply and demand in regular DRAM. NAND upgrades from 2xx to 3xx and 4xx layers continue; the CEO cited Lam's talk of $40 billion over multiple years of NAND upgrade investment, and said customers see a 22% CAGR for AI-specific memory (2 to 3x the regular memory market).
memory shortage until 2028 (per customers' customers); $40 billion multiyear NAND upgrade (Lam, as cited by the CEO); AI-specific memory 22% CAGR (per customers)

Q4 2025 segments: Materials Solutions sales were $362 million, flat year over year and up 4% sequentially. Advanced deposition materials drove most of the sequential growth, helped by demand for moly deposition in NAND. The segment's adjusted operating margin was 20.9%. Advanced Purity Solutions sales were $465 million, down 5% year over year and up 1% sequentially. Fluid Handling and FOUPs drove the year-over-year decline, partly offset by strong growth in liquid filtration, which had another record quarter. The APS adjusted operating margin was 24.8%. The CFO said the year-over-year margin decline came from costs related to ramping the Taiwan and Colorado manufacturing sites and lower production volumes, and the sequential decrease from unfavorable product mix and the timing of operating expenses.

Materials Solutions $362 million (flat YoY, up 4% sequentially), adjusted operating margin 20.9%; Advanced Purity Solutions $465 million (down 5% YoY, up 1% sequentially), adjusted operating margin 24.8%

NAND: the move from roughly 250 layers to approximately 300 layers is under way. Management expects more than 20% NAND bit growth in 2026, driven mainly by higher-layer, higher-capacity NAND rather than a big increase in wafer starts. Entegris expects a double-digit increase in its NAND content per wafer as customers move to higher layer counts and adopt new materials such as moly and selective etch. It has won strong POR positions in NAND deposition materials, CMP and selective etch. NAND utilization is around 85%, and layer-count increases are absorbing most of the remaining 15% of capacity, with fewer new wafer starts. If demand stays strong, flash makers will likely need to add significant fab capacity, setting up higher NAND MSI growth in 2027. The CEO said Entegris gains from both layer growth and wafer growth, with slightly more from a full wafer start.
more than 20% NAND bit growth expected in 2026; double-digit increase in NAND content per wafer; NAND utilization around 85%

name: OCS
note: Optical Circuit Switch — Google's all-optical interconnect. ASP $50k-$200k. MEMS dominant (mass production). Players: Lumentum, Coherent, Innolight (SiPh OCS 2027), Accelink, Robotechnik.

tables.title: OCS adoption & milestones
rows: Google TPU v4 — first OCS supercomputer (4,096 chips, 48 OCS)
Google TPU v7 SuperPod — OCS interconnects 9,216 chips

1.6T optical-module PCB: current orders are mainly 1.6T high-speed optical-module boards; 2026 optical-module related revenue is guided to double, 1.6T keeps growing sharply in 2027 and becomes the main shipping spec in 2028, and 3.2T boards are already being sampled. Customers are already pre-booking 2027 capacity; target is to become the world's largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027. 800G-and-above optical-module boards require M7-class ultra-low-loss laminate (1.6T effectively mandates it); management says roughly 20 players claim to be entering optical modules but few master M7 high-layer board production, which is why Zhen Ding's substrate-derived M7 technology gave it the 1.6T breakout. 1.6T optical-module board yield is described as industry-leading at above 90%, including the newly ramped Thailand lines. On a potential US FCC ban on Chinese optical modules: Zhen Ding supplies the PCB inside the module, not the module itself, so sees no direct hit, and can shift production to Thailand where customers require it. On CPO: the company says it will participate in both pluggable and CPO/NPO architectures as they develop; most PCB equipment is transferable between product types so a CPO shift would strand little capacity.
2026 optical-module revenue to double; 1.6T main spec by 2028; 3.2T sampling; 1.6T board yield above 90%; goal: largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027

Data Center revenue was a record $137.6 million, up approximately 40% sequentially, driven by 800G and 1.6T PAM4 demand. The segment grew 35% in 2024 and 48% in 2025 and is trending toward about 74% THIS YEAR. The primary driver from fiscal 2025 to 2026 is 200-gig PAM4 products in pluggable optical modules; ZR and ZR-light are growing over 100% year over year; 100-gig-per-lane single mode and multimode are posting high double-digit growth; and legacy 25-gig-per-lane products for 100G FR and LR4 are also growing strongly. Book-to-bill within Data Center is driven primarily by 1.6T and 800G platforms. MACOM is sampling its latest generation 200G and 400G PER LANE TIAs and drivers. A structural tailwind: hyperscalers are moving from PASSIVE COPPER TO FIBER in scale-up applications, which is pure SAM expansion for MACOM because it does not promote passive copper solutions.
Data Center revenue $137.6M (+~40% QoQ, record); segment growth 35% in 2024, 48% in 2025, ~74% trending this year

NPO and XPO positioning: MACOM has BETWEEN 10 AND 20 ACTIVE NPO DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS across various customers and use cases, and expects some of that revenue to kick in IN 2028, with NPO starting to grow significantly from 2028. Critically, MACOM says it will NOT build or supply optical engines - in Data Center it is a chip supplier, not a multichip assembly or module supplier. It describes the architectural evolution as pluggable transceivers with DSPs, to LPO platforms that remove the DSP, morphing into smaller package-less NPO platforms; those architectures still need drivers and TIAs, but with much higher density - smaller parts, more channels, lower power, and varied form factors using wire bonds, bumped devices or flip chip, plus through-silicon-via options. Because these solutions are specific to the architectures hyperscalers are driving, the design wins come directly to MACOM. Related applications include LPO and LRO on single mode or multimode.
10-20 active NPO development projects; NPO revenue expected to begin in 2028

Indium phosphide is the key medium-term lever. 200-GIG PHOTODETECTORS are ramping in volume production and becoming a meaningful contributor to Data Center growth; 400-gig photodetectors are in the hands of perhaps a dozen customers with very positive feedback. The 75-MILLIWATT CW LASER qualification continues: MACOM is well into HTOL testing (typically 5,000 hours) with data described as exceptional, is gaining confidence but cannot yet declare success, and is developing plans for a POTENTIAL START TO PRODUCTION IN LATE CALENDAR 2027, scoping modest capex and fab space for a rapid high-volume ramp for a few strategic customers. CEO Steve Daly called bringing a CW laser into production in 2028 'a watershed moment' that could be a very large revenue contributor. Separately, demand for MACOM's 25G DFB lasers (100G QSFP, CWDM4, LR4) is rising with urgency because of a GENERAL SUPPLY SHORTAGE OF INDIUM PHOSPHIDE DFB LASERS. MACOM expects to gain meaningful indium phosphide market share over the next three years; its Ann Arbor, Michigan facility has built photodiodes for over a decade and grows its own epitaxy by MBE.
200G PDs ramping in volume; 400G PDs at ~a dozen customers; 75mW CW laser potential production start late calendar 2027

Total data-center revenue is expected to grow about 69% from approximately $591 million in calendar 2025 to about $1 billion in calendar 2026. The exposure spans PCIe Gen6 switches and retimers, storage and NVMe controllers, timing and synchronization, Ethernet switches and PHYs, optical modules, security and memory.

Microchip had 14 PCIe Gen6 design wins as of the call: 12 switch programs and two retimer programs spanning both scale-up and scale-out at hyperscaler and enterprise customers. Gen6 entered production at the end of June, but none of the 14 wins was yet shipping in volume; management expects significant data-center growth in 2027 and thereafter.
14 PCIe Gen6 wins (12 switch, 2 retimer); production began end-June; volume ramps ahead

THE NPO / SCALE-UP THESIS AND THE III-V ROADMAP: SiPho pluggables (800G/1.6T) have 'for the most part ALREADY REPLACED COPPER for scale-out connections outside the rack'; the NEXT FRONTIER IS SCALE-UP, where Tower has SEVERAL NEAR-PACKAGED-OPTICS (NPO) DEPLOYMENTS PLANNED OVER THE NEXT YEAR and many more in design — NPO expected to be 'in the TENS OF PERCENT' of SiPho shipments by H2 2027 (it reuses the pluggable ecosystem, easing hyperscaler reliability/serviceability/multi-source concerns). Content growth comes from HETEROGENEOUS INTEGRATION: III-V-on-silicon INTEGRATED InP LASERS (several tens of $M of revenue expected in 2027; chip-to-wafer bonding moving in-house), die-to-wafer/wafer-to-wafer bonding, and next-gen modulators (400G/lane silicon with Coherent; TFLN and InP in development); multi-year IQE EPI SUPPLY AGREEMENT resolved the InP-substrate crunch. SiGe: 100G/200G-per-lane drivers and TIAs in HVM across all three 200mm fabs (pluggables + LPO/LRO), 400G/lane next with tight EIC-PIC co-design. Adjacent read-through: image-sensor demand SURGING for machine-vision inspection driven by 'the accelerated build-out of DDR and HBM MEMORY ASSEMBLY LINES.'
NPO = tens-of-% of SiPho shipments by H2-2027; integrated InP lasers = tens of $M in 2027; pluggables already displaced copper for scale-out

→ Coherent: Joint OFC announcement with Coherent of a 400G-PER-LANE MODULATOR IN SILICON — the next-generation figure-of-merit work (alongside Tower's thin-film lithium-niobate and InP modulator development) that anchors multi-generation exclusivity-style engagements.

Silicon photonics revenue reported within comms infrastructure and data center is now expected to MORE THAN DOUBLE in 2026 versus the prior year. GF secured 7 new optical networking design wins in Q2 across both pluggable transceiver suppliers and major hyperscaler and networking players, and is actively engaged with 4 OF THE TOP 5 optical transceiver players. Pluggables contribute the vast majority of silicon photonics revenue today. High-volume manufacturing of 200-gig-per-lane technology is underway, 400-gig capability has already been demonstrated, and the multiyear roadmap advances module enablement to 1.6T, 3.2T and beyond. GF has more than 40 silicon photonics customers, and CEO Tim Breen said GF is on track and potentially ahead of the growth targets set for end-2028 through 2030. He also cited an expectation that 70% of data center links will be optical by 2030, calling that 'perhaps even conservative' given scale-up as well as scale-out penetration.
Silicon photonics revenue to more than double in 2026; 7 new design wins in Q2; engaged with 4 of top 5 transceiver players; >40 SiPho customers; 200G/lane in HVM, 400G/lane demonstrated

Silicon germanium is OVERSUBSCRIBED THROUGHOUT 2027 and, notably, GF's SiGe business is LARGER THAN ITS SILICON PHOTONICS BUSINESS TODAY. GF secured multiple new SiGe TIA and driver design wins across networking customers in the quarter. The growth has two compounding drivers: the shift to optical networking itself, and the fact that what could previously be done in CMOS at 50-gig and 100-gig per lane cannot be done at 200-gig and definitely not at 400-gig per lane, forcing transimpedance amplifiers and increasingly the drivers out into high-performance analog processes like SiGe. High-performance analog also appears in near and co-packaged optics depending on architecture. GF is expanding SiGe capacity at Burlington, Vermont and qualifying 300-millimeter SiGe in Singapore for additional capacity, better economics and higher fT/fMAX performance. The SiGe lineage traces to IBM Microelectronics, which invented SiGe and is part of GF today.
SiGe oversubscribed throughout 2027; SiGe business larger than silicon photonics today; Vermont capacity expanding, 300mm SiGe qualifying in Singapore

CALL-ONLY: NEOCLOUDS ARE 'GOING LONG' IN 100G/400G WAVES - THE CLEAREST CARRIER-SIDE AI SIGNAL IN THE QUARTER. Strategic WAVES revenue (100G and 400G) grew nearly 11% YoY in North American enterprise, and strategic WAVES SALES were up nearly 35% YoY - management called the sales number 'a nice precursor to future revenue'. CEO Johnson attributed it to share gain, not market growth: 'the neo clouds go long in 100 and 400 gig'... 'Yes, we're taking share', enabled by RAPIDROUTES turning up circuits 'in days, versus what used to take months' and by the density of '58 million fiber miles'. Neocloud PCF deals are 'relatively small' - neoclouds are buying WAVES, not conduit ('That is a part of the Waves growth... that's how they're choosing to buy their net connectivity'). Framing of the cycle: the uptick in 100G/400G 'is indicative of the SECOND PHASE OF THE AI ADOPTION CURVE, where more customers are starting to realize that they've got to upgrade their capacity', while legacy low-bandwidth wave circuits decline. Separately, satellite backhaul is a growing fiber-demand source - 'data needs to find fiber as fast as possible. We do the backhaul for the satellite companies and it's growing pretty significantly'.
100G/400G waves revenue +11% YoY, SALES +35% YoY; 58M fiber miles; neoclouds buying waves not PCF

448G SerDes development progressing well with a co-packaged copper system solution, IP expected ready in the second half of next year; beyond 448G the roadmap most likely needs to go optical, and MediaTek continues to develop CPO system solutions on TSMC's COUPE platform for next-generation system connectivity, plus an end-to-end 3.5D platform (IP, packaging, design flows) and industry-leading D2D IPs.
448G SerDes IP ready second half of next year (2027)

Strong new orders predominantly driven by optoelectronics — 75% of Q2 equipment orders; the key driver is the architectural shift in AI data centers from copper towards high speed optical connectivity at 800G and eventually 1.6T and beyond; a diversified set of almost 15 laser companies makes up about 80% of order intake, from Europe, the U.S., Taiwan, Japan and China; around EUR 200 million quarterly order intake expected for the coming quarters
Q2 orders EUR 215 million; ~EUR 200 million quarterly order intake expected going forward

The limiting factor is ramp rate, not capacity — how fast AIXTRON and its suppliers can hire and train people; output ramping 3X within the year (EUR 59 million Q1 to over EUR 200 million implied in Q4); customer advance payments fund the ramp
advance payments EUR 197 million at end of June, around 43% of the equipment order backlog, more than EUR 150 million above year-end 2025

Customers are increasingly standardizing on the G10-AsP platform for advanced photonic devices (yield, uniformity, cost of ownership); near-term demand driven by indium phosphide EMLs and CW lasers for data centers, with customers already working on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) as the next step; roughly 70%-80% of systems ship configured for 4-inch wafers, prepared for 6-inch conversion; initial 80-120 tools per year opto market view now seeing stronger momentum than that

DEMAND DRIVERS AND CUSTOMERS: optical connectivity deployment in AI data centers is accelerating 'as hyperscalers scale GPU dense architectures and look for higher speed lower power photonics'. Near term the pull is the industry migration to 1.6T transceiver modules, 'for which indium phosphide based lasers and detectors are essential'; longer term, hyperscalers advancing toward NEAR-PACKAGED AND CO-PACKAGED OPTICS 'will continue to drive increasing demand for our material' — pointing to a durable multiyear demand cycle. AXT signed strategic LONG-TERM SUPPLY AGREEMENTS with COHERENT and another partner, and announced one with LUMENTUM the week of the call. US cloud/AI capex is the primary driver for EML and silicon-photonics transceivers plus high-speed photodetectors; AXT believes its material is used at MULTIPLE US HYPERSCALERS with end-customer use expected to broaden, alongside 'huge growth in China'. Corporate: subsidiary Tongmei withdrew its STAR Market IPO application (06-26-2026) and is redirecting to a HONG KONG EXCHANGE listing (~1 year); this created a redemption right on $49M of 2021 PE investment, though those investors currently wish to remain.
1.6T migration + CPO/NPO drive multiyear InP cycle; LTAs with Coherent and Lumentum; Tongmei to HKEX

Photonics: customers ramping production of high-speed optical transceivers for 800G and beyond; SEMI's pluggable optical transceiver solutions revenue almost tripled year-on-year in H1 2026, with further growth expected for the rest of 2026. CPO is still small, with the packaging-equipment inflection point seen between 2027-2028, more likely 2028; ASMPT's portfolio (Amicra ultra-high-precision bonders, TCB, hybrid bonding, flip chip mass reflow) covers EIC/PIC integration, optical assembly and fiber attach.
pluggable optical transceiver revenue approximately $75 million in H1 2026, almost tripled year-on-year

AI Data Center applications rose from 59% to 61% of revenue (+20% QoQ; vs 47% a year ago, +71% YoY). BT capacity is being selectively converted: memory-controller BT demand stays strong while lower-end consumer BT lines are wound down or converted toward ABF-class work.
ABF 52% of revenue (+22% QoQ, +51% YoY); AI Data Center 61% of revenue (+71% YoY); AI over 60% of substrate revenue in H1, potentially 70% in H2; PCB AI share 60%+ going to 65-70%

Engagements cover high-speed connectivity as customers move to 800G and 1.6T, with precision timing demand rising alongside data rates and rack density.
AI data-center growth >50% annually; 800G/1.6T connectivity and precision timing

Networking cadence: 1.6T mass production ramps commence in Q3 2026 with two hyperscaler customers; 10 active 1.6T programs 'really surging' in 2027 with additional awards likely in coming quarters; 400G 'remarkably resilient' from 2026 into 2027 alongside strong 800G growth. 1.6T MP from Q3 2026; 10 active 1.6T programs; CPO samples 1H27, MP 2H27

HPE is the FIRST OEM to productize a Broadcom Tomahawk-6-based, 100% liquid-cooled switch (1.6 Tbps, 'HelioStack' reference architecture, introducing in fall 2026), with a roadmap extending through co-packaged optics for lower power. Scale-up (Helios switch) + scale-out (QFX fabric) + scale-across (PTX DCI) covered.
First Tomahawk-6 liquid-cooled switch; Networks-for-AI >= $2B FY26

Booked $1.8B in new AI systems orders, bringing cumulative AI systems bookings to $16.4B; entered Q3 with $5.9B AI backlog (primarily enterprise + sovereign). Networking (Juniper integrated, ahead of plan) revenue $2.7B (+10% normalized); raised cumulative FY2026 Networks-for-AI order target to at least $2B. First OEM to productize a Broadcom Tomahawk 6-based 100% liquid-cooled switch; QFX AI scale-out fabric; Juniper PTX 800G scale-across; co-packaged-optics roadmap. AI systems bookings $16.4B cumulative; Networks-for-AI target >=$2B

12-inch German fab equip install Q2 2026; SiC 750V->1.7kV; 800G/1.6T switch passives

Q1 rev NT$70.1B +64% YoY; record 400G/800G switch shipments

Interconnect power (optical modules / CPO): Tony Balow said MPS has seen great growth in optical modules over the past year and a half and treats the market as 'interconnect', with engagements for CPO and active copper as well; 'we would expect optical module to continue to grow as you start to see the 1.6 ramp', and communications should be a growth area in 2026 on both optical modules and data center switches. optical module growth expected with the 1.6 ramp; CPO not a 2026 revenue driver

800G coherent pluggable ramp (CEO): 'In Optical, our 800-gig ZR and ZR+ pluggable products are shipping with initial units performing well in the field. We now have multiple design wins and are supplying into scale deployments. Our focus is on ramping production to meet the strong demand we see in the market.' In Q&A: 'We're ramping on 800-gig multiple pluggable wins, as we've talked about, a lot of active customer conversations on that space'.
800-gig ZR and ZR+ pluggables shipping; multiple design wins; supplying into scale deployments

Scale-across and speed transitions (CEO): scale-across data center interconnect is 'one of the most significant near term' drivers of optical demand. 'We've gone through the 400- and 800-gig transition very quickly.' 'we expect that 1.6 and 3.2 will come. And when you look at that scale across is the tailwind for both the technology transitions and the demand. And then, of course, over time, we see scale out increasingly be an opportunity for coherent optics.' Scale-across is also a tailwind for routing ('switching is much more about the data center racks, the spine-leaf architecture'). Later: 'Scale across is an emerging opportunity' and 'over time, as speeds continue to ramp within the data center, there will be more opportunity for coherent optics within the data center.' He described 'a much more mature and larger optical market, driven by the AI infrastructure build-out than we've seen in the past.'
400- and 800-gig transition passed very quickly; 1.6 and 3.2 will come; coherent optics moving toward scale out / inside the data center over time
